items.followUp: How do cancer cells form secondary tumours in other parts of the body?

rubric.why: Metastasis is the spread of cancer cells away from the original tumour.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that cancer cells spread from the original tumour.

rubric.why: Metastasis can result in secondary tumours at other locations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the spread can form secondary or new tumours in other parts of the body.

modelAnswer: Metastasis is the spread of cancer cells from the original tumour to other parts of the body, often through the blood or lymph.
These cells may form secondary tumours at the new locations.

items.followUp: What structure forms between daughter cells during plant-cell cytokinesis?

rubric.why: The phragmoplast helps form or position the cell plate between the daughter cells.
rubric.description: Formation or positioning of the cell plate
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the phragmoplast helps form or position the cell plate.

rubric.why: The cell plate develops into a partition that separates the daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the developing cell plate forms a partition separating the daughter cells.

modelAnswer: The phragmoplast helps form and position the cell plate between the daughter cells.
The cell plate develops into a new partition, separating the daughter cells.

rubric.why: Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining karyokinesis as nuclear division.

rubric.why: Karyokinesis results in two daughter nuclei.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that karyokinesis forms two daughter nuclei.

modelAnswer: Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus during cell division.
It results in the formation of two daughter nuclei.

items.followUp: How does an extreme pH affect the shape and activity of an enzyme?

rubric.why: High temperatures or extreme pH can cause enzyme denaturation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying high temperature or extreme pH as a condition that can cause denaturation.

rubric.why: Denaturation changes the enzyme's shape, so the substrate no longer fits properly.
rubric.description: Change in shape and substrate fit
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the enzyme or active site changes shape, preventing the substrate from fitting properly.

modelAnswer: Denaturation of an enzyme can occur at high temperatures or at an extreme pH.
The enzyme's shape, especially its active site, changes, so the substrate no longer fits properly.
